scope: How to treat ClinicalTrials.gov trials labelled PHASE2+PHASE3 (seamless)
notes: Excluded from the main duration set; kept in data/processed/durations_combined_sensitivity.csv
rationale: A seamless trial's duration cannot be attributed to Phase 2 or Phase 3 alone; keeping it separate lets us test sensitivity without contaminating single-phase estimates

scope: How to treat ClinicalTrials.gov trials labelled PHASE1+PHASE2
notes: Excluded from the main duration set; kept in data/processed/durations_combined_sensitivity.csv
rationale: Same reason as PHASE2+PHASE3; Phase 1/2 trials also include a safety component not present in Phase 2

scope: Restrict CT.gov trials to industry sponsors
notes: Lead sponsor class = INDUSTRY; collaborators are ignored
rationale: BIO and Wong (industry tables) measure industry programs; matching the sponsor scope keeps durations and success rates describing the same population

scope: Which date rule defines the main duration sample
notes: Main: rule d = completed, untyped dates treated as ACTUAL, start year 2010-2019 (data/processed/durations_main.csv). Sensitivity: rules a (all years), b (strict ACTUAL), c (2011-2020) in durations_rule_{a,b,c}.csv, and completed+terminated (docs/filter_log.md). ESTIMATED dates excluded under all
rationale: Rule d medians lie between rules a and b; no era trend across 2005-2019; excluding 2020+ starts avoids right-censoring (long recent trials not yet completed)

scope: Day used when CT.gov gives only YYYY-MM
notes: Day 15 imputed; imputed counts in docs/filter_log.md
rationale: Mid-month minimises the maximum error (about +/-0.5 month) and is unbiased if the true day is uniform

notes: Exclude duration <= 0 months, < 1 month, or > 180 months (15 years); excluded rows saved to data/processed/durations_excluded.csv
rationale: Non-positive durations are data-entry errors; < 1 month is too short for a Phase 2/3 efficacy trial (mostly single-dose/PK studies); >15 years is implausible for one Phase 2/3 trial. Exclusion (not winsorizing) because these values are errors, not extreme-but-real observations

notes: Method: trial duration = primary completion - start, completed industry single-phase trials, resampled in the simulation. Values in data/processed/duration_summary.csv; docs/filter_log.md. Date rule d (ASSUMPTION_DATE_TYPE_ACTUAL_ONLY)
rationale: Only public source of observed start/completion dates at scale. Trial duration is a proxy for phase duration (see ASSUMPTION_TRIAL_TO_PROGRAM)

scope: Mapping from individual CT.gov trials to drug development programs
notes: CT.gov is trial-level; BIO and Wong rates are program-level. No official crosswalk. Trial duration is used as a proxy for phase duration, which ignores parallel trials and gaps between trials

scope: Duration of the submission/review step (BIO NDA_APP gate) and of review time inside Wong P3_APP
notes: Review time = FDA_PDUFA_PRIORITY_NME (8 months) with probability p_priority, else FDA_PDUFA_STANDARD_NME (12 months). p_priority is ASSUMPTION_P_PRIORITY. Wong P3_APP time = Phase 3 duration + review time
rationale: CT.gov has no regulatory review dates; PDUFA goals are the official FDA targets. Goals are met for 90% of applications and are targets, not observed review times

scope: Share of applications receiving priority review (p_priority)
notes: Value not filled. Sensitivity range: p_priority in {0, 0.5, 1}. Passed to the model as a parameter, never hard-coded. Reference (not a model input): FDA CDER 'New Drug Therapy Approvals 2023' (https://www.fda.gov/media/175253/download) printed p.11 (PDF p.13): '31 of the 55 drugs (56%) approved in 2023 were designated as Priority Review'. Two biases if used: (1) share among APPROVED novel drugs, not among submissions (rejected applications are missing); (2) CDER only, CBER biologics excluded. The yearly web lists (Novel Drug Approvals for YYYY) have no priority-review column
Not modelled: one review period per submission. BIO NDA_APP (90.6%) counts eventual approval including resubmissions, so approved timelines that needed a resubmission are understated

scope: gap_months: time between phases, added twice on the path (Phase 2 end -> Phase 3 start, Phase 3 end -> submission)
notes: Default 0 (base case, timelines biased short). Sensitivity range: gap_months in {0, 3, 6}. No source used

scope: review_extra_months: extra time added to every review period on top of the PDUFA goal
notes: Default 0. No sensitivity range set. No source used

scope: When a failing asset stops accruing time
notes: Cumulative time runs to the end of the gate at which it fails (e.g. Phase 2 failure = Phase 2 duration only)
rationale: Project instruction; the failure is observed when the phase's trial reads out

scope: Cost per phase (clinical trial direct cost)
notes: Base case: ASPE14_COST_P2_MEAN and ASPE14_COST_P3_MEAN (Table 2 weighted means, role=base). Sensitivity: Table 1 lowest/highest therapeutic area (ASPE14_COST_P{2,3}_{MIN,MAX}_AREA, role=sensitivity). Costs are fixed, not sampled. A phase's cost is paid on entering the phase, whether it then succeeds or fails: Phase 2 always, Phase 3 only after passing Phase 2. Total = trials_per_phase x overhead_multiplier x cpi_factor x sum of phase costs
rationale: ASPE does not publish trial-level variance (its SD is across therapeutic-area means), so there is no sourced distribution to sample from. Spending varies through which gate each asset reaches

notes: Not counted: no cost is charged at NDA_APP (BIO) or for the review part of P3_APP (Wong). ASPE14_COST_NDA_FEE (PDUFA filing fee only) stays CANDIDATE / reference
rationale: Project decision: the cost scope is clinical trial direct cost

scope: trials_per_phase: number of trials run per phase (ASPE costs are per trial)
notes: Default 1. Sensitivity: 1 and 2. No source used

scope: cpi_factor: price-level adjustment applied to ASPE nominal 2004-2012 dollars
notes: Default 1.0 (no adjustment: results in mixed-year nominal dollars). No source used

scope: overhead_multiplier: sponsor costs not captured by ASPE trial costs
notes: Default 1.0. Sensitivity: 1.5 and 2.0. No source used

scope: Which source provides the base-case phase transition probabilities
notes: BIO 2011-2020 is the main scenario; Wong 2019 is the sensitivity scenario. Never mixed within one run
rationale: BIO has a separate submission->approval gate and a period (2011-2020) closer to the CT.gov duration sample; Wong uses a different method (path-by-path) and database, so it serves as a robustness check

scope: Split of Wong P3_APP into Phase3->NDA and NDA->approval
notes: No split: Wong scenario uses two gates, Phase 2->3 (P2_P3) and Phase 3->approval (P3_APP)
rationale: Wong reports Phase 3->approval only; splitting it would add an input with no source. Project scope defines the Wong scenario as two gates

scope: Independence of phase outcomes and of programs within a pipeline
notes: Each transition is treated as independent given the program reached that phase; programs sharing a target, platform or company are treated as independent of one another

scope: Historical success rates apply to future programs
notes: Both sources are historical (2000-2015, 2011-2020); applying them forward is an assumption

method: Per-study cost from itemized Medidata contract data
data_period: 2004-2012 contract data, nominal USD (not inflation-adjusted); published 2014
notes: One trial; nominal US dollars; 2004-2012 contract data; U.S. trials; no allocation of failed programs' costs. SD $2.51M (weighted SD across therapeutic-area means; see SD DEFINITION); Per-study cost: one trial per phase, NOT a whole program, and NOT inclusive of failures (p.3-2, PDF p.29; Table 1 note [b]). Includes 25% site overhead and a 30% 'All Other Costs' extrapolation; undiscounted. SD DEFINITION: p.3-4 (PDF p.31): 'we computed a weighted mean cost ... and its weighted standard deviation ... where the weights are the total number of contracts'; the formula runs over therapeutic-area means (sum over therapeutic areas of the reported mean minus the across-area average). Table 2 note (p.3-6): 'the reported numbers represent weighted average costs and standard deviations'. So the SD is the contract-weighted spread of therapeutic-area MEAN costs across areas: neither the SD between individual trials nor the standard error of the mean. Trial-level variances were supplied by Medidata (p.2-9) but are not reported. FAILURES: p.3-2 (PDF p.29): 'Table 1 presents the total costs for each of the therapeutic areas included in our model by clinical trial phase (assuming one trial per phase and not inclusive of failures).' Meaning: the figure is the cost of one trial and is not grossed up for the trials of programs that fail (contrast p.4-1: DiMasi et al. estimates 'represent fully capitalized costs and are inclusive of failures'). Sample: the report does not say the trials completed or succeeded. Costs are built from negotiated contracts (PICAS/CROCAS, p.2-9) times PLANNED patients and sites (p.3-1), i.e. budgeted cost per trial regardless of outcome; whether early-stopped trials are in the database is not stated. CURRENCY/YEAR: nominal US dollars, mixed years. p.2-9: 'The data are from 2004 and later and have not been adjusted for inflation by Medidata ... we were unable to adjust them for inflation'; p.2-10 gives the range of the itemized cost data as 2004-2012 (only the revenue figures were inflated to 2008 dollars). U.S. trials only (p.2-9). Report landing page: https://aspe.hhs.gov/reports/examination-clinical-trial-costs-barriers-drug-development
rationale: Base-case phase cost (ASSUMPTION_PHASE_COST)
